pages.text: Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) Skip Navigation Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) September 2026 The Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) is an experimental data product extending the set of statistics published by the Business Dynamics Statistics (BDS) program. The BDS-SU-REV provides year-over-year changes in employment, payroll, and revenue for each quarter of the year for businesses that operate in one location (single-units) and file their taxes under a single Employer Identification Number (EIN). This product relies on IRS annual tax filings to collect revenue information and IRS quarterly tax filings to collect employment and payroll information for the pay periods including March 12 th , June 12 th , September 12 th , and December 12 th . Year-over-year employment and payroll changes are calculated between the same point in year t and year t-1 (i.e., June 12 th year t-1 to June 12 th year t, etc.). Employment and payroll growth is labeled as job and pay creation respectively and employment and payroll decline as job and pay destruction. A novel innovation in the BDS-SU-REV is the incorporation of annual revenue data for single-establishment firms that consistently maintain positive employment levels each quarter. A positive annual growth in revenue is categorized as revenue creation, while negative growth is categorized as revenue destruction. Jump to: Data Definitions

pages.text: Business Expenses Supplement (BES) Business Expenses Supplement (BES) Skip Navigation Within About Business Expenses Supplement (BES) Purpose The Business Expenses Supplement (BES) produces detailed operating expenses estimates for retail businesses located in the United States. Previously, the BES also produced national estimates for accommodation and food service firms in the United States. Beginning with the 2016 survey year, however, the accommodation and food service data are now collected and published through the Service Annual Survey (SAS) . Frequency The supplement is conducted every five years. Specifically, it occurs in years ending in "2" and "7," just like the Economic Census . Coverage The estimates include data only for retail businesses with paid employees (that are located in the United States). Content All businesses that receive the BES are asked to provide data on their total and detailed operating expenses for the year being collected. In particular, businesses must submit data related to their annual payroll before deductions, purchased electricity, purchased advertising and promotional services, etc. The BES questions are added to the Annual Retail Trade Survey (ARTS) survey questions in years ending in “2” and “7.” Products Estimates are released approximately 15 months after the reference year has concluded and are published at an industry level. The industries used in the BES data products stem from the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) . The survey provides local, state, and federal officials near real-time data for policy and decision-making including after natural disasters or during economic crises. The BTOS also provides insights into business recovery after these events. The BTOS sample consists of approximately 1.2 million businesses split into six panels (approximately 200,000 cases per panel). Businesses in each panel are asked to report once every 12 weeks over the course of one year. Data collection occurs every two weeks. The BTOS is comprised of a set of core questions and supplemental content, which is added as needed. The BTOS collects information on a broad range of business conditions. Topics include current performance, changes in revenue, employment, hours worked, demand, and prices. For most concepts, businesses are asked about the previous two weeks and for a 6-month outlook. Data collected from September 11, 2023 to present include all employer businesses (single location and multi-location) in the U.S. economy, excluding farms. BTOS data are released every two weeks and are available by 2022 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) sector, by state and for the 25 most populous Metropolitan Statistical Areas. pages.description: Peter Bradshaw: Reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes.
pages.text: But I'm a Cheerleader | Movies | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Movies This article is more than 25 years old Review But I'm a Cheerleader This article is more than 25 years old Peter Bradshaw Thu 12 Apr 2001 21.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google D irector and co-writer Jamie Babbit makes her feature debut with this satire of America's creepy Christian "sexual reorientation" camps, where confused teens are sent so that their nascent gayness can be deprogrammed out of them. Natasha Lyonne plays Megan, a cheerleader who hugs her fellow pom-pom-botherers inappropriately and hates making out with her jock boyfriend. He and Megan's family arrange an "intervention" where she is confronted with her shameful tendencies and sent to the True Directions camp, run by two smug tyrants in Straight Is Great T-shirts, played by Cathy Moriarty and RuPaul (here out of drag), clearly repressed gays themselves. Once there, Megan falls for a girl with the interesting name of Graham, played by Clea DuVall. As in all therapy boot-camp movies - such as Girl, Interrupted, in which DuVall had a role - there has to be a wild child with whom the heroine makes a connection. This is Graham's role. It's reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes. But it could have been funnier, and I would have preferred to know more in documentary terms about the actual reality of these terrible camps, rather than sit through this heavy-handed and oddly lenient comedy. pages.description: Whether it’s a short hop across the Channel or an overland expedition to the furthest reaches of Europe, some of the richest travel experiences happen when you skip the flight.
pages.text: By Land and Sea—17 European Trips From London | National Geographic By Oliver Smith Published October 24, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Today, it’s easier to travel further and faster around Europe than ever before — to board a flight and effectively parachute yourself into a new destination. But by travelling overland, be it by ferry, train or car, on a bike or on foot, you’re able to observe the slow, subtle changes at ground level with every accumulated mile. Overland travel by rail is also easier than it’s ever been, thanks to an ever-expanding network of high-speed and sleeper trains across Europe. You might board a morning Eurostar at London St Pancras International and that same day be joining a midnight crawl of Madrid’s tapas bars or standing beneath Milan’s hulking Duomo as stars twinkle above its white marble facade. Ferries, too, offer perspectives unfamiliar to those at the cruising altitude of an airliner, whether that’s witnessing the green coast of northern Spain unravelling out of the blue horizons of Biscay or seeing Icelandic volcanoes peek over grey North Atlantic waves. Radiation standards at the facilities are primarily used to calibrate portable surface gamma-ray survey meters and borehole logging instruments used for uranium and other mineral exploration and remedial action measurements. Standards for calibrating borehole fission neutron devices are also available, but are used infrequently. Radiation standards are constructed of concrete with elevated, uniform concentrations of naturally occurring potassium, uranium, and/or thorium. Pad standards have large, flat surfaces suitable for calibration measurements with portable surface survey meters. Borehole standards are large concrete cylinders with 4.5-inch-diameter test holes. And NIST is also the place to go if you need to calibrate your measuring equipment. In our everyday lives, calibrations are often the little adjustments you may make, for example to make sure the colors of your computer monitor or television are accurate, so it will show photos or videos the way that a filmmaker or photographer intended. But for a scientific measurement laboratory such as NIST, calibrations are a bit different. NIST calibrations determine a relationship between the measurement standard (like the Kibble balance) and that instrument or object (such as a cylindrical metal kilogram mass). By using a world-class reference such as the Kibble balance, calibrations make it possible for a piece of measuring equipment to make the most accurate measurement it can. From MRIs to lasers, NIST's calibration services are part of many aspects of everyday life. Stout comes to the BLM from the U.S. Forest Service where he served as Forest Supervisor of the Eldorado National Forest in the Central Sierras of California. Before his tenure with the United States Forest Service, Stout held leadership positions at all levels of the BLM. This historic route stretched thousands of miles across the West, turning travelers’ dreams and Native American ways of life into destinies marked by both gain and loss. Between 1841 and 1869, thousands of pioneers traveled nearly 2,000 miles from the Missouri River to the Sierra Nevada Mountains and beyond. Driven by hopes of fertile land, religious freedom, and gold, their journey was far from easy. Despite these hardships, people kept coming, lured by the promise of prosperity and adventure. His dizzy turn was put down to high blood pressure caused by dehydration. "I didn't know what it was, I looked at the board and I just felt like everything was spinning," Menzies told BBC Scotland. The site provides outdoor recreation opportunities in a non-motorized natural setting for 400,000 to 500,000 visitors annually. The 25-mile trail system winds through the woods, providing year-round recreation opportunities on unpaved trails that link to the adjacent 4,000 acre Far North Bicentennial Park trail network managed by the Municipality of Anchorage Parks and Recreation Division (MoA). Popular activities include walking, running, mountain biking, horseback riding, and wildlife viewing. In the winter, activities include snowshoeing, fat tire biking, skijoring, and cross-country skiing. pages.text: Can a Controversial Diet Help Treat a Hidden Cause of Migraines? | National Geographic Premium HEALTH Can a Controversial Diet Help Treat a Hidden Cause of Migraines? Migraines have long been linked to blood sugar levels that are too high or too low—but for some people a different kind of metabolic dysfunction might be the real culprit. Mounting evidence suggests some people with chronic migraines might be experiencing rapid swings in blood sugar levels, a condition known as reactive hypoglycemia. Seeking relief, some have turned to the keto diet—which drastically cuts out carbohydrates to force the body to produce non-glucose fuel sources. She had spent the last six years cycling in and out of the hospital, trying one new medicine after another and cutting out various foods to identify potential triggers, yet was still averaging 28 migraine days a month. “I was spending most of my days in bed, wearing sunglasses or hats inside,” Mead says. pages.text: Can AI save the Maldives’ coral reefs? | National Geographic By Jessica Vincent Published September 11, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). I should be watching my dive buddy, but I’m distracted by a giant clam. It’s electric blue mottled with black swirls, like ink dispersing in water. John Jay Rouse | St. Cloud, Minnesota Much of what we know about which colors insects can see is based on a combination of behavioral studies and understanding the morphology and physiology of the insect eye. The compound eye found in most insects is made up of a few to thousands of individual units called ommatidia, and each ommatidium includes a rhabdom, a transparent structure under the lens, which stores photosensitive pigments known as opsins that are used for detecting colors. The more kinds and combinations of opsins an insect’s rhabdom has, the more colors it can see. Most insects can only see a narrow spectrum of colors, if any at all. March 3, 2025 Cancers Caused by HPV Key points HPV infections can cause certain cancers in men and women. HPV vaccination can prevent over 90% of cancers caused by HPV. Talk to your child’s doctor about getting HPV vaccine to prevent HPV infections. Why it's important HPV can cause cancers of the: Cervix, vagina, and vulva in women Penis in men Anus in both men and women Back of the throat, including the base of the tongue and tonsils (oropharynx), in both men and women Cancer usually takes years, even decades, to develop after a person gets HPV. There is no way to know who will develop cancer or other health problems from HPV. People with weakened immune systems (like people living with HIV/AIDS) may be less able to fight off (clear) HPV infections, and more likely to develop health problems caused by HPV. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Canyons of the Ancients National Monument Canyons of the Ancients National Monument, located in the Four Corners region of southwestern Colorado, protects a stunning cultural landscape with the highest known density of archaeological sites in the United States. Encompassing 176,000 acres of public lands, the Monument features more than 8,300 documented sites—including villages, kivas, field houses, cliff dwellings, petroglyphs, and ancient roadways—with estimates suggesting over 30,000 yet to be recorded. These sites offer a window into over 12,000 years of human history, primarily shaped by Ancestral Puebloan cultures and their descendants. The area continues to be a living landscape used today for traditional purposes, recreation, hunting, livestock grazing, and energy development. It also encompasses Cross Canyon , Sego Lily, and Cahone Canyon Wilderness Study Areas. While exploring the Monument’s canyons, mesas, and desert terrain, visitors are reminded to Visit with Respect and Leave No Trace to protect the resources that define this unique place.
